  continuo abandon <issue URL> [directory]

cli.main.usage:
continuo — turns a GitHub Projects v2 kanban board into a work queue and has Claude Code work through the issues.

Usage:
  continuo [flags]               start the daemon (with no arguments, reads WORKFLOW.md in the current directory)
  continuo <subcommand> [args]

Subcommands:
  init [directory]                write a WORKFLOW.md template
  setup [directory]               map the kanban board's Status options to continuo's five roles (interactive)
  doctor [directory]              check that everything is in place
  trust [directory]               trust target repositories with Claude Code (--dry-run to preview)
  abandon <issue URL> [directory]
                                 put an issue that was started by mistake back the way it was before it started
  allow-keychain-access          allow reading the macOS Keychain once
  version                        print this binary's version
  hook                           called by Claude Code hooks (not meant to be run by a human directly)

Flags:
cli.setup.board_err: Could not read the kanban board's Status field: %v
cli.setup.board_err_owner: Could not determine the kanban board's owner (%s)
cli.setup.board_err_project: Could not determine which kanban board to use (%s)
cli.setup.board_remedy_generic: → Fix what the message above says, then run it again.

cli.setup.err_keys_not_rewritable_remedy: → Write that key's value on one line (example: active_states: ["Ready", "In Progress"]), then run it again.
cli.setup.err_not_a_directory: Error: %v. continuo setup takes the directory that has WORKFLOW.md.
cli.setup.err_not_found: %s does not exist. continuo setup only rewrites the Status mapping in an existing WORKFLOW.md (it does not ask about any role mapping on its own).
cli.setup.err_not_found_remedy: → Run continuo init first to create WORKFLOW.md.
cli.setup.err_owner_invalid: Error: %q given for --owner is not accepted as a GitHub user/organization name (must start with an alphanumeric character and contain only alphanumerics and hyphens, at most 39 characters)

workspace.prepare.branch_in_use_elsewher:
%[1]w (branch: %[2]s / worktree currently using it: %[3]s). **Only one worktree can check out a given branch, so starting as-is will always make `git worktree add` fail.**
How to check: Run `git -C %[4]s worktree list` to see which worktree has that branch checked out.
Common causes: A worktree from a previous run is still left over elsewhere, or a human created a worktree for the same branch by hand.
What to do: Run `continuo abandon %[5]s`. This cleans up that issue's worktree and branch together. If you do not want to lose any work still there, check its contents first with `git -C %[6]s status`.
workspace.prepare.branch_mismatch:
%[1]w: %[2]s has %[3]q checked out (expected %[4]q)
How to check: git -C %[5]s status
Common causes: the issue body pointed at another branch and the agent switched to it / a new branch was cut to open a second PR for the same issue
What to do: First check whether there are uncommitted changes and commits that have not been pushed.
        If you need the work on the current branch, switch back to the expected branch and merge it there.
        If the expected branch still exists: git -C %[6]s switch %[7]s
        If the expected branch is gone: git -C %[8]s switch -c %[9]s
Note: Do not run continuo abandon. It destroys the work inside the worktree.
        Even without --force it can move Status to failure_state when the conditions line up.
workspace.prepare.clone_not_found:
%[1]w. **The polling loop never clones on its own** (so it never pulls in a repository just because it appeared on the kanban board, without permission).
How to check: Run `ghq list -p -e %[2]s/%[3]s`. Zero lines means it is not present locally.
What to do: Make sure `trust.repositories` in WORKFLOW.md includes `%[4]s/%[5]s`, then run `continuo trust`. It fetches the clone and registers trust together.
workspace.prepare.detached_head:
%[1]w: %[2]s
How to check: git -C %[3]s status
        If it says `rebase in progress`, finish or abort it first (`git rebase --abort`).
        If it says `bisecting`, run `git bisect reset` to get back.
Common causes: a commit was checked out directly / a rebase is in progress / a bisect is in progress
What to do: First check whether there are uncommitted changes.
        If the expected branch still exists: `git -C %[4]s switch %[5]s`
        If the expected branch is gone: `git -C %[6]s switch -c %[7]s`
        git refuses `git switch` during a rebase. Finish that first.
Note: Do not run `continuo abandon`. It destroys the work inside the worktree.
        Even without --force it can move Status to failure_state when the conditions line up.
